Affiliation:: Department of Psychology, Arizona State University
Data & Platforms: RMSEA (Root Mean Square Error of Approximation)
Application Areas: Clinical Psychopathology Assessment and Scale Refinement
Psychometric Model Validation and Structural Equivalence
Key Research Thinking Patterns: Simulation-Based Robustness Testing: Quantifying the stability of latent variable models under non-normal conditions using Monte Carlo simulations and Fleishman’s Power Method to derive empirical cutoffs for fit indices.

Dynamic Fit Index Framework: Developing and applying the Dynamic Fit Index (DFI) to evaluate model fit sensitivity, moving beyond static benchmarks to assess practical equivalence in structural equation modeling.

Information-Theoretic Scale Optimization: Utilizing Multidimensional Item Response Theory (MIRT) and Item/Test Information Functions to identify redundant items and enhance the precision of clinical instruments like the Duke Misophonia Questionnaire.

Empirical-Theoretical Structure Alignment: Conducting rigorous cross-model comparisons between theoretical factor structures and empirical data via Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA) and Target Rotation to ensure measurement parsimony and replicability.
Summary Description: Patrick Manapat is a psychometrician specializing in Item Response Theory (IRT), Exploratory Factor Analysis (EFA), and research integrity. His work quantifies the robustness of latent variable models under nonnormality using Monte Carlo simulations and develops the Dynamic Fit Index (DFI) framework. Expanding into clinical psychometrics, he applies Multidimensional IRT (MIRT) and information functions to refine complex clinical scales, such as the Duke Misophonia Questionnaire. He focuses on distinguishing theoretical from empirical factor structures to enhance measurement precision and parsimony. His research bridges methodological taxonomy and applied scale validation, ensuring that psychometric tools maintain practical equivalence and replicability across diverse clinical populations.
